title: Combined Gulf river silica-to-nitrate load estimates rose by 23% from 1980-1996 to 2009-2025, but source limits permit a decline
abstract: We tested the annual silica-to-nitrate load ratio at the Mississippi and Atchafalaya outlets with USGS version 3.0 estimates. The combined stationary flow-normalized molar ratio rose from 1.100 in 1980-1996 to 1.349 in 2009-2025, a 22.61% point increase. Silica loads rose by 9.70% and nitrate plus nitrite loads fell by 10.53%. Both rivers and all three load methods had positive point changes. However, a box formed from annual marginal source limits permits a combined change from -4.41% to +59.24%. This is not a joint confidence interval. Adverse changes of 5.09% in each of four period mean loads can remove the point increase. A shorter recent period has a positive box minimum, so the box result also depends on period choice. The main change remains uncertain. This fixed-version comparison extends established silica-ratio work with two-river accounting and explicit source-error sensitivity. It does not test coastal nutrient limitation, physical cause or ecosystem recovery. Code, the CC0 source, all comparisons, a figure, hashes and a separate arithmetic audit are included.

display.caption: Point ratios and changes in USGS load estimates. Lines in the right panel are marginal-limit sensitivity boxes, not joint confidence intervals. K has no source limits.
